strengths: Setting hyperparameters in DP optimization is an important topic for both modeling and privacy.

Experiments demonstrate the advantage of the proposed method compared to naively applying parameter free optimization methods like D-adaptation in DP optimization, and DP-hyper style algorithm by differentially privatizing hyperparameter search.
The proposed algorithm works pretty well in the experiment with not much additional cost in computation cost and privacy.
The idea is simple yet effective, factorizing learning rate tuning during training using quadratic approximation.
Hyperparameter selection in DP does not inherit the same rules of thumb as non-DP, and hence understanding hyperparameter selection for DP training is a core problem.
The results are strong and seemingly near optimal (given the non DP grid search results).
The observation that a specific generic ML hyperparameter selection approach translates well to the DP setting seems important and novel to the DP community.
This is a well-written paper that effectively presents its methods.
The connections to previous work are discussed.
The experimental results are comprehensive and convincing.
The method is simple yet effective in terms of efficiency and utility.
The theoretical results are presented clearly, avoiding unnecessary complications.
weaknesses: The technical part of the paper is generally hard to read.
I am not confident the proposed method is technically correct.

The authors need to clarify the relationship to GeN Bu et al. (2023), the missing Eq (5), and explain what ω in Eq (5) and (6) is, and provide (or justify absence of) a closed-form solution for estimating η.

I request the authors to clarify privacy accounting of their proposed method, including mechanism input and output, composition of “Loss Privatization” and “Gradient Privatization”, and how data-dependent steps like Line 9 in Algorithm 1 are considered in DP accounting, as well as details on using GDP/autoDP for this algorithm.
Minor: the authors might consider the usage difference of \citep and \citet in writing.
The proposed algorithm seems to still require an initial learning rate and the algorithm's sensitivity to the initialization seems missing.
The presentation can be improved; there are possible typos and issues with claims that could be resolved with changes to writing.
Certain details about the experimental setup are missing, such as exact DP δ values used, and the range of hyperparameter grid search.
